name: Honeybadger
summary: Honeybadger is an error and uptime monitoring service that catches crashes in your app and also tells you when the app itself goes down.

free_plan_covers.note: The free Developer plan includes 5,000 errors a month, 1 uptime monitor and 1 user, free forever.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The Team plan is $26/month (or $286/year) for 50,000 errors a month, 5 uptime monitors and unlimited team members.

portability.note: Honeybadger's exception SDK is proprietary, but it also accepts OpenTelemetry data over the standard OTLP protocol, so existing OpenTelemetry tracing can be pointed at Honeybadger directly.

uptime_checks.note: Uptime Monitoring checks your app from outside on a schedule from multiple locations and alerts you when it goes down; the free plan includes 1 monitor.

session_replay.note: Honeybadger has no session replay; it covers error tracking, uptime and cron monitoring, logging and status pages instead.

setup.step: Create a free Honeybadger account and a new project to get its API key.
Install Honeybadger's SDK for your framework (@honeybadger-io/js covers plain JavaScript and Node).
Configure Honeybadger once where your app starts, in server code and in the browser, reading its settings from your environment.
Add your API key, deploy revision and assets URL to your environment file.
Upload source maps on every build with Honeybadger's bundler plugin, and add its error boundary or error handler around your app so crashes get reported.

builder_notes: The Honeybadger API key is write-only and meant to be public in browser code, unlike a typical secret key; it can only send error reports in, not read data out.
Upload source maps and set the revision on every build, or stack traces won't map cleanly back to your source.
There's no session replay, so pair Honeybadger with a separate tool if you need to see what a user did before an error, not just the stack trace.
